Advanced Information Extraction from Smartphone-Captured Medical Documents

Internship progress report — IMT / PTIT Hanoi Supervisor: Thanh-Ha DO · Report date: 5 August 2026 · Week 3 of 12

Summary

The goal is a pipeline that turns a smartphone photo of a Vietnamese medical invoice into structured, verified data. Three weeks in, the core is built and measured, and the deliverables planned for weeks 1–8 are complete.

TEDS header fields multi-page merge
Chandra OCR 2, adaptive 0.966 29/32 100 % / 100 %
HunyuanOCR-1.5, adaptive 0.953 28/32 100 % / 100 %
PaddleOCR-VL, adaptive 0.951 24/32 100 % / 100 %
PP-StructureV3 0.557 9/32 100 % / 100 %

All four models are measured by one command — scripts/eval_all.py — with the same ground truth, so the columns are strictly comparable. The evaluation code itself has been improved since the first figures circulated (Markdown table parsing, three ground-truth corrections); every number in this report was re-measured under the current code.

Two contributions go beyond the original plan.

Multi-page table merging. Vietnamese pharmacy invoices routinely spill a single medication table across two or three pages. Every model reads each page in isolation, so the table comes back cut in pieces. The merging step reassembles it at 100 % precision and 100 % recall, with zero wrong merges across eight benchmark runs.

Adaptive extraction. An invoice is arithmetically redundant — every line satisfies quantity × unit_price = total, and the lines sum to the printed grand total. That redundancy lets us score an extraction without any ground truth, which is the situation in production. The pipeline reads each page twice, scores both readings, and keeps the one that holds up. On twelve invoices the policy had never seen, it beats both single readings and lands 0.003 from the best achievable choice.

A working prototype exists: a Progressive Web App that takes a photo, shows every step of the chain, and returns JSON.

1. The problem, and the constraint that shapes everything

The subject targets smartphone photographs, explicitly excluding native PDFs. That single constraint drives the whole design: the input is warped, its lighting is uneven, its resolution varies, and the page boundary must be found before anything else can happen.

A second constraint is legal. Real patient invoices cannot be collected, and even if they could, they carry personal health data. Working on them at internship scale is not an option.

The consequence: build the ground truth rather than find it

No public dataset exists for photographed Vietnamese medical invoices with exact ground truth. We generate one.

JSON (patient, doctor, medication list)
  → LaTeX with longtable, which splits long tables across pages by itself
  → PDF → PNG
  → Blender projects each page onto a curved 3-D mesh, with a real
    background and realistic lighting

This gives something no real photograph can: the exact answer is known before the photo exists. Blender also writes a UV map next to every render, whose first channel is a pixel-perfect mask of the sheet — so even the page-localisation step can be scored exactly.

Two independent ground truths are maintained, and keeping them separate is a methodological point rather than a detail:

  • the generator JSON says what the invoice contains — it feeds table scoring, arithmetic validation, and field evaluation;
  • the source PDF says where the invoice breaks across pages — it feeds the merge evaluation.

Deriving page grouping from OCR output would mean grading the merging algorithm on the very data that inspired it.

2. Measuring: TEDS

We use TEDS (Tree-Edit-Distance-based Similarity, Zhong et al., PubTabNet 2020), the standard metric for table recognition. Using the published metric rather than a home-grown score means these numbers are directly comparable to the literature — and it removes any suspicion that the metric was chosen because it flattered the result.

How it works

An HTML table is a tree: table → tr → td, with the text in the leaves. TEDS measures the minimum number of edit operations — insert, delete, rename a node — needed to turn the predicted tree into the expected one, then normalises:

TEDS = 1 − edit_distance / max(nodes_predicted, nodes_expected)

The detail that matters: renaming a cell does not cost 1, it costs the normalised edit distance between the two strings. Reading 500mq instead of 500mg is therefore nearly free, while losing the cell entirely is not.

Measured on a three-line reference table (demo/explain_teds.py reproduces this in one second, no model required):

error introduced TEDS TEDS-Struct naive cell accuracy
perfect reading 1.000 1.000 1.00
one wrong character 0.998 1.000 0.96
one damaged diacritic 0.989 1.000 0.96
one empty cell 0.967 1.000 0.96
one column lost 0.867 0.867 undefined
one row missing 0.767 0.767 undefined

Two properties are visible at once.

It grades. A wrong character, an empty cell and a lost row do not cost the same, and they rank in the right order. A binary metric would price all three identically.

The second column isolates the kind of error. TEDS-Struct stays at 1.000 as long as only text is wrong, and drops as soon as the grid breaks. That is what let us say PP-StructureV3's bottleneck is character reading rather than table detection — a 0.300 gap between the two columns.

Why not simple cell accuracy

It becomes undefined the moment a row or a column is missing, because it compares cells at matching positions and there are no longer matching positions. That is precisely the most common OCR failure on a table. TEDS stays defined in every case.

What it says about multi-page tables

On the same reference table, reading the first page perfectly — while the invoice continues on a second — scores 0.533. Two thirds of the table are simply absent. That is the ceiling for any system that reads pages in isolation, and it is measurable without running a single model.

3. Model comparison

Four models were evaluated on the same 17 warped pages: HunyuanOCR-1.5 (1 B parameters), PaddleOCR-VL (0.9 B), PP-StructureV3, and Chandra OCR 2 (5 B). Chandra does not fit in the laptop's 4 GB of VRAM; its runs were produced on a rented Kaggle T4 (kaggle/bench_kaggle_chandra.ipynb), in fp16 — the T4 has no hardware bf16 — at roughly 81 s per page.

Raw reading, one bar pair per model:

model size TEDS TEDS-Struct gap s/page
HunyuanOCR-1.5 1 B 0.950 0.973 0.023 ~87 (laptop GPU)
Chandra OCR 2 5 B 0.916 0.943 0.027 ~81 (Kaggle T4)
PaddleOCR-VL 0.9 B 0.909 0.933 0.024 ~230 (CPU)
PP-StructureV3 — 0.557 0.857 0.300 ~60 (CPU)

The most instructive result is still PP-StructureV3's 0.300 gap between TEDS and TEDS-Struct. It reconstructs the grid well but reads Vietnamese characters poorly: the bottleneck is character recognition, not table detection. That single observation ruled out an entire family of classical pipelines for this language.

On raw warped pages, five times more parameters do not buy first place. Chandra 2's public benchmarks predicted this: its Vietnamese score (80.4 %) sits below its own 43-language average and regressed from Chandra 1 — the version 2 gains went to other languages. We wrote that prediction down before running the benchmark (docs/chandra_ocr2.md), and it held.

With pre-processing, the ranking flips. Chandra turns out to be the model that benefits most from the flattened, illumination-corrected input: 0.916 → 0.966, against 0.950 → 0.879 for HunyuanOCR (whose pre-processed run predates the current pre-processing code — a caveat that also means its adaptive figure is a floor rather than a ceiling). Under the adaptive policy, which needs no ground truth, Chandra ends at 0.966 with 29/32 header fields — the best multipage result of the four — and at 0.977 (ceiling 0.977) on the twelve deformed invoices of the diversified set, where HunyuanOCR has not been run and PaddleOCR-VL reaches 0.942.

On the flat diversified set Chandra reads 47/48 header fields and reaches 0.981 of TEDS against 0.976 for PaddleOCR-VL.

Two Chandra-specific defects are worth naming, because the metrics alone hide them. Its HTML tables occasionally carry a malformed header (colspan/rowspan misplaced, one column absorbed) — visible on the very first multipage page. And its arithmetic-validation recall is 80 % rather than 100 %: one of its misreads shifted a whole line by one column in a way that still multiplies correctly (1700 × 6800 = 11 560 000), the only kind of numeric error the arithmetic check is structurally blind to. Neither defect affects the merge decisions, which stay at 100 % precision and recall across all five Chandra runs.

4. Multi-page table merging

This is the internship's main technical contribution, and it answers a specific remark from the supervisor.

Why it is hard

Every OCR model reads one page at a time. When a medication table spans pages, the model returns two tables, each with its own header, and the page-break artefacts in between: a repeated header row, a -- Tiếp trang trước -- continuation banner, a Xem tiếp trang sau... footer.

Recognising a continuation is not obvious, because two consecutive invoices from the same pharmacy look almost identical: same column template, same header text, same fonts.

How the decision is made

The algorithm combines several signals rather than trusting one:

signal what it means
continuation marker on page B the document says so explicitly
numbering continuity page A ends at 19, page B starts at 20
B starts above 1 the numbering came from somewhere
A ends with a grand total the invoice is closed
B restarts at 1 a new numbering is a new document
compatible shape same column count, or similar header

Two of these act as vetoes: an invoice that ends on its grand total, or a table that restarts at 1, closes the document. A continuation marker on the next page overrides both — that is the document asserting the continuation rather than us inferring it.

Results

run precision recall
HunyuanOCR-1.5 100 % 100 %
HunyuanOCR-1.5, pre-processed 100 % 100 %
PaddleOCR-VL, pre-processed 100 % 100 %
PP-StructureV3 100 % 100 %
diversified set, flat 100 % 100 %
diversified set, warped 100 % 100 %

Zero wrong merges across every run. That is the number that matters most: a missed continuation costs some TEDS, but a wrong merge fabricates a table mixing two different patients' invoices — and nothing downstream can detect it, because each line still balances arithmetically.

Merging is worth +0.26 to +0.34 of TEDS depending on the model. On the diversified set, where five invoices carry no continuation marker at all, the gain reaches +0.34: that figure quantifies what the algorithm recovers when the document itself signals nothing.

5. Pre-processing — the Phase 1 deliverable

The module locates the sheet, flattens it, evens out the lighting, and denoises. Unlike a dewarping oracle, it knows nothing about the deformation — it estimates everything from the image alone, which is what a real application must do.

Sheet localisation is scored exactly against the Blender UV masks. The naive approach — thresholding plus contour detection, the literal reading of the subject's Phase 1 — reaches IoU 0.44 and produces zero usable crops. It latches onto the table border rather than the paper edge, because on a printed invoice the highest-contrast rectangle is the table. A naive pre-processing module would therefore have cropped away the header — hospital, patient, date, doctor — while appearing to work.

GrabCut brings this to 0.79 by modelling colour distributions instead of thresholding one cue. Measurements show why that matters: comparing the sheet region against the background across our renders, brightness, saturation and texture each flip sign from one image to the next.

A second opinion with the ink erased brings it to 0.90, and the rule behind it is checkable rather than tuned: erasing the ink cannot move the edge of the sheet, so the two readings should agree. When the second is much larger, the first was locked onto printed content.

What pre-processing actually buys

On the original test set it lifts HunyuanOCR from 0.950 to 0.973 and PaddleOCR-VL from 0.909 to 0.951.

It also recovers information that was entirely lost. On one page, the raw OCR output contains no patient, date or doctor block at all — not misread, absent. On the pre-processed image, all three lines appear. That answers a question left open for a week: the fields were being lost to the deformation.

But it is not free. On the warped diversified set, pre-processing taken alone degrades the result — 0.906 → 0.879 — and header fields collapse from 42/48 to 24/48, because the crop clips the sheet edge on some pages and PaddleOCR-VL's layout analysis discards a partially cut text line entirely.

The right way to read this: pre-processing is not a replacement for the raw reading, it is a safety net. It rescues pages that drop out, at the cost of new losses elsewhere. Which leads to the next section.

6. Arithmetic validation, without ground truth

An invoice checks itself. Every line satisfies quantity × unit_price = total, and the lines sum to the printed Tổng tiền.

On 215 line items read by HunyuanOCR, 12 lines are flagged (6 %), and they contain 100 % of the numeric errors, with zero false alarms. That is what makes a TEDS of 0.97 usable in practice: a human reviewer is shown six per cent of the document, not all of it.

Two honest limits:

  • Name errors are invisible to arithmetic by construction. Nothing in the invoice reveals that Xetoprofen should read Ketoprofen. Catching those would need a medication dictionary — a separate and complementary avenue.
  • When two of the three numbers are right, the third can be recomputed. The pipeline does this and marks the line corrected rather than silently overwriting it.

7. Adaptive extraction

The validation score above needs no ground truth. That makes it usable for something else: ranking two candidate readings of the same photograph.

The pipeline reads each page twice — raw and pre-processed — scores both, and keeps the one that holds up. Table and header fields are decided independently, because they fail independently.

The policy was designed and tuned on the original 8 invoices. Applied unchanged to 12 invoices, 6 layouts, warped — data it had never seen — it beats both single variants on both metrics and lands 0.003 from the ceiling.

Why it wins is visible in the detail:

invoice confidence raw / pre-processed kept TEDS raw TEDS pre-processed
9 1.00 / 0.75 raw 0.905 0.509
12 1.00 / 0.75 raw 0.960 0.580
1 0.60 / 1.00 pre-processed 0.828 0.957

On two invoices pre-processing collapses, and the ground-truth-free score sees it. On a third, pre-processing rescues a page that had dropped out, and the score sees that too. This is the clearest validation of the principle: an invoice's internal redundancy is enough to detect an extraction disaster where no ground truth exists — which is exactly the production situation.

8. Does any of this generalise?

The original test set is 8 invoices from one template, where the STT column restarts at 1 in every invoice. That is precisely the assumption the most discriminating merge signal rests on. A test set that respects it everywhere cannot put it in doubt.

So a second set was built: 12 invoices, 25 pages, 6 layouts, varying numbering mode, continuation marker, column count (5, 6 or 7), border style, and presence of the total row. Five invoices number continuously across invoices — the adversarial case, where the end of one invoice and the start of the next look exactly like a page continuation.

It found real defects.

Two in the algorithm. With continuous numbering, invoice N ending at 32 and invoice N+1 starting at 33 were merged into one — the worst failure available. And when OCR lost a page entirely, a rescue branch merged across an invoice boundary. Both are fixed, both are covered by tests/test_merge_assumptions.py, which runs in one second without any model.

Three in the measurement itself. The page-grouping reference keyed on the continuation marker — one of the very signals the merge algorithm uses. The expected-table builder hard-coded six columns and numbering from 1. These made a 5-column invoice score 0.836 when it actually scored 0.974.

The pattern is worth stating plainly, because it generalises beyond this project: each widening of the test set broke the measuring instrument before it measured anything. A benchmark built on a single template does not only validate the algorithm too little — it validates its own reference too little, and the agreement between the two proves nothing.

The cost of deformation, isolated

The same 12 invoices exist flat and warped, same content, same layout. Only the deformation changes.

Deformation costs −0.070 of TEDS (0.976 → 0.906) but only −0.020 of structure (0.986 → 0.966). It damages character reading far more than grid reconstruction — consistent with what PP-StructureV3 showed earlier.

And the effect is binary, not gradual: nine invoices lose under 0.07, three lose more than 0.11. Either the page survives or it drops out. That is a measured argument for pre-processing: its job is not to shave hundredths off easy pages, it is to bring dropped pages back into the regime where the model works.

9. The application

A Progressive Web App, backed by a FastAPI service. Photo in, verified table and JSON out.

The interface deliberately exposes every step, because a demonstration should show reasoning and not just a result:

step what is shown
reception the pages submitted
pre-processing the detected quadrilateral drawn on the photo, its score, the flattened image
reading progress, page by page
merging for each transition, merged or separate, and the signals that decided it
validation each line coloured by status: ok, corrected, inconsistent, incomplete
adaptive choice the confidence of each reading, and which was kept

Two design decisions worth naming:

Compute stays server-side. The models are gigabytes; the phone photographs, the server reads. This also allows changing model without redeploying anything to devices.

The second reading is conditional. Paying for two readings on every photo doubles the wait, and it is often useless — on the diversified set, the raw reading already scored 1.00 on five invoices out of twelve. The API reads the raw image, scores it, and only pays for the second reading when that score doubts. It is the adaptive idea applied to compute time rather than accuracy.

A replay mode re-runs an already computed result instantly, which is what should be used in a meeting: nobody watches a frozen screen for three minutes.

10. Eight silent failures

Not one of the following raised an error. Every one was found by comparing against a reference, and this is the most concrete argument in favour of the whole evaluation apparatus.

failure effect how it was found
torchvision image backend HunyuanOCR emitted 6842 characters of gibberish in 315 s output inspection
English prompt (official, verbatim) triggered layout analysis instead of parsing — perfectly well-formed output, answering another question comparing output shapes
Vietnamese đ NFKD does not decompose it, so ĐVT never matched dvt and the unit column was lost from every parsed invoice field-level evaluation
mirrored columns one page returned right-to-left with no header; the export produced a plausible empty invoice explicit extraction status
Markdown tables HunyuanOCR sometimes answers in Markdown, not HTML; the parser discarded the whole page, content intact page-level audit
footer prose bác sĩ appears as an ordinary word in the legal footer, filling the doctor field with a sentence reading extracted values
non-deterministic GrabCut five identical calls returned areas 0.504, 0.413, 0.021, 0.021, 0.021 — the module was not reproducible repeat measurement
NumPy 2.x PaddleOCR replaced the real ImportError with "a dependency error occurred during pipeline creation", naming neither package nor exception full traceback

The thread connecting them: nothing crashes, everything appears to work. Only confrontation with a reference reveals the problem. This deserves a section of the final report in its own right.

11. Limitations

Stated plainly, because they will be the first questions asked.

All data is synthetic. 20 invoices, 7 layouts, 42 pages — one generator, one deformation engine. No real photograph has been processed. The planned remedy is to print the fake invoices and photograph them, which keeps the exact ground truth that no real document allows. It is blocked on printer access, not on method.

Sample size. The adaptive policy holding on a set it had never seen is a genuine indication of generalisation, but twelve invoices is twelve invoices.

A TEDS of 0.97 still leaves roughly 3 % of cells wrong. On medical invoices, this is not shippable without human review. The arithmetic validation makes that review cheap — six per cent of lines — but it does not remove it.

The application is a prototype. It has no authentication and no encryption, and it carries patient names. It must not leave a local demonstration network. Photo grouping, page ordering, capture-time quality control and manual correction are all missing.

12. Licensing and ethics

HunyuanOCR is released under the Tencent Hunyuan Community License, whose Territory excludes the European Union, the United Kingdom and South Korea. Development and deployment in Vietnam are compliant. Two restrictions apply everywhere: outputs may not be used to train another model, and the acceptable use policy restricts automated decisions in medicine.

This has a practical consequence already encountered: compute platforms whose region cannot be chosen — Kaggle and Colab among them — are a licensing risk.

PaddleOCR-VL is Apache 2.0 with none of these constraints. That is a selection criterion that does not reduce to accuracy, and it deserves an explicit decision rather than a default.

Chandra OCR 2 sits in between: Apache 2.0 code, weights under a modified OpenRAIL-M — free for research and for organisations under $2 M of funding/revenue, no geographic restriction. Unlike HunyuanOCR it can be run on region-less platforms such as Kaggle without licensing risk, which is exactly how its benchmarks here were produced. Given that it also posts the best adaptive score, the model choice is now a genuine three-way trade-off between accuracy, hardware cost (5 B does not fit the laptop GPU) and licence.

Next steps, in order of value

  1. Image degradation study — motion blur, sensor noise, JPEG compression, under-exposure. Pure software, produces the week 9–10 deliverable, and tests a hypothesis nothing else can: does pre-processing pay off more as quality drops?
  2. Real photographs — print and shoot. The most predictable criticism of the whole work.
  3. Anonymisation (Phase 4) — not started; connects directly to the ethics discussion above.
  4. Free-text NER — the current corpus is almost entirely tabular; the generator needs enriching first for the task to mean anything.
